escena.titulo: Why the numbers aren't the answer

turnos.t: If Option A has the higher net gain, why might a manager still choose B?

Because the numbers aren't the whole answer. Probabilities are estimates, often optimistic. If the new shop fails, it returns 60,000 euros on an 80,000 cost: a 20,000 loss, for a business with only 90,000 in cash.
It still gains 10,000. So a risk-averse owner may choose B. Decision trees also leave out qualitative factors, like staff, the brand and the owners' time.
